dict.string: The macos command reads and edits your contacts only when you run a contacts command in the terminal.
The macos command reads and edits your calendar events only when you run a calendar command in the terminal.
The macos command needs full calendar access to list, create and delete events for the calendar commands you run.
The macos command reads and completes your reminders only when you run a reminders command in the terminal.
The macos command needs full reminders access to list and complete reminders for the reminders commands you run.
The macos command controls apps such as Safari, Mail, Messages, Music and Finder only for the commands you run.
The macos command reads your current location only when you run the location command in the terminal.
The macos command asks for your location while it runs a location command, and never in the background.

Informational only — macOS provides no Info.plist key that requests or grants Full Disk Access. Some commands (Apple Notes, Messages history, Safari data) read protected databases and therefore require Full Disk Access, which you must grant to this binary yourself in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access. See docs/SIGNING.md.
